subject: About fitting random slope model and using half-t prior

messages.author: 2d2a4f5aa0df3ec7
messages.subject: About fitting random slope model and using half-t prior
parts:
Hi developer team,

Happy holidays and thank you for the great maintenance of the package all this time.

I have a question regarding fitting random slope models. Code as below:
HT.prior = "expression:
sigma = exp(-theta/2);
nu = 3;
log_dens = 0 - 0.5 * log(nu * pi) - (-0.1207822);
log_dens = log_dens - 0.5 * (nu + 1) * log(1 + sigma * sigma);
log_dens = log_dens - log(2) - theta / 2;
return(log_dens);
"
h.t = list(prec = list(prior = HT.prior))

model <- inla(outcome ~ State + TxARM + f(State, TxARM, model = "iid",
                                          , hyper = h.t,
                                          constr = TRUE),
              data = sample_data,
              lincomb = lc,
              family = "pom",  
              verbose=FALSE, control.compute = list(config=TRUE))

I want to use half t distribution for my hyperparameter(hierarchical variance of state variable). There are two levels for State and 2 levels for TxARM. However, I got error as attached. I am wondering if I am specifying my model wrong or if there is any other problem.

Another question is, I am wondering if it is possible to specify a scale parameter for the half t distribution (so specifying both scale and degrees of freedom). I could not figure out a proper way to do so. 

Thank you in advance and have a great day!

Best,
Jocelyn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] About fitting random slope model and using half-t prior
parts:
seems like you have two ','s in f() terms, so this works

n <- 100
State <- rnorm(n)
TxARM <- rnorm(n)
outcome <- rnorm(n)

data = data.frame(outcome, State, TxARM, State2 = State,
TxARM2 = TxARM),
verbose=FALSE, control.compute = list(config=TRUE))


well, you need to rename State as you can only use it once...
